task.description: REWORK ITERATION 1 (implementation side -- the design itself already passed re-validation): implement §13.2/§13.3 of the validated design (lib/letflow/design/iss-0048-sandbox-pool-owner-crash-reclaim.md) -- add a one-sentence claim/2 @doc addition and a short moduledoc paragraph stating the same-process claim/release contract (doc-only, claim/2's @spec itself does not change). Then restructure test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:192-221 (the 'a queued waiter is served once the held slot frees' test) per §13.4's send/receive rendezvous shape: the Task.async-spawned process must itself call release/2 after handing its claim result back to the test process, rather than the test process calling release/2 on a claim it never itself made. Your prior implementation of the owner-monitor mechanism in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex (commit ef1e4c8, already on this branch) is correct and does not need to change -- this rework is doc additions plus the test restructuring only.

result.summary: Added the §13.2 claim/2 @doc sentence ('The process that calls claim/2 must be the same process that later calls release/2...') and the §13.3 moduledoc '## Same-process claim/release contract' paragraph to lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex -- doc-only; `git diff` confirms claim/2's @spec (lines below the new @doc text) is byte-identical to before, only @doc/@moduledoc prose was added. Restructured the 'a queued waiter is served once the held slot frees' test (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs) per §13.4: the Task.async body now claims, sends {:waiter_claimed, claim} to the test process, blocks on `receive` for a :release_waiter_claim signal, then itself calls SandboxPool.release/2 for that claim before returning the claim struct; the test process asserts via assert_receive, sends the release signal, and asserts on Task.await's return -- release now happens from the same process that claimed, eliminating the owner-monitor false-positive reclaim. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> 'Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated letflow app', clean, zero warnings. `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` run 3x: run 1 '7 tests, 0 failures' (Finished in 2.8s), run 2 '7 tests, 0 failures' (Finished in 2.8s), run 3 '7 tests, 0 failures' (Finished in 3.2s) -- stable 3/3, no flake. mix format --check-formatted flagged the restructured test block's line-wrapping (plus one pre-existing, unrelated finding in a different test file); ran `mix format` scoped to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs only, re-verified compile+3x test pass after reformatting.
